title: Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

reading.body:
An autonomous vehicle operated by Avride struck and killed a duck in Austin while in autonomous mode, with a human safety operator present but not intervening. The vehicle did not slow down or stop before impact. This is a failure of the autonomous driving system to detect and avoid a small animal in its path, despite having a human monitor onboard who could have taken control.

Whether the vehicle also failed to stop at a stop sign is not established. Avride disputed residents' claims after reviewing its data, and no independent verification of this allegation is noted in the reporting. The incident shows that current object detection in autonomous vehicles may not reliably identify small animals as obstacles requiring avoidance, and that human safety operators may not consistently intervene in edge cases.

Avride responded by removing streets around the area from service and running simulated tests to improve detection. Catching this failure before deployment would have required testing the vehicle's behavior around wildlife and validating that small animals trigger appropriate stopping responses in real-world conditions.

summary:
# Summary

An autonomous vehicle operated by Avride struck and killed a mother duck in the Mueller Lake neighborhood of Austin, Texas, prompting significant community backlash. The incident occurred when the self-driving car, which had a human safety operator on board, hit the duck without slowing down or stopping. Residents were particularly upset because they knew the duck personally, as it had been nesting in a pot outside a local Italian restaurant. Some neighbors also claimed the vehicle failed to stop at a stop sign, though Avride disputed this assertion after reviewing vehicle data.

Following the incident, Avride confirmed the vehicle was in autonomous mode at the time of the collision. The company has adjusted its testing operations by excluding certain streets around the lake from its service area. Avride is now conducting simulated experiments to improve its technology and prevent similar situations in the future while maintaining safety performance. Local residents have rescued the duck's eggs and placed them in an incubator. Multiple autonomous vehicle companies, including Waymo, Tesla, and Zoox, continue testing or operating in Austin.
